questions.q:
Match the reagents in List - I with products obtained from their carbonyl compounds in List - II.
List - I: (a) NH$_2$OH (b) R-NH$_2$ (c) R-OH (d) H-C$\equiv$N
List - II: (i) Cyanohydrin (ii) Oxime (iii) Schiff base (iv) Acetal
options: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv
questions.explanation: NH$_2$OH gives an oxime, R-NH$_2$ gives a Schiff base (imine), R-OH gives an acetal, and HCN gives a cyanohydrin with carbonyl compounds.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde + Acetophenone $\xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-/293K}$ gives the major product 'A' via a base-catalysed condensation. [Options show drawn structures.]
options: Ph-CH=CH-Ph (a stilbene, with no carbonyl retained)
A benzene ring bearing both -CHO and -COCH$_3$ substituents (para-disubstituted)
Ph-CO-CH$_2$-C$_6$H$_4$-CHO (a ketone joined through -CH$_2$- to an aryl aldehyde)
Ph-CH=CH-CO-Ph (chalcone, formed by aldol condensation of the two carbonyls with loss of water)
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so acetophenone's enolate attacks its carbonyl carbon (crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation); dehydration gives the conjugated chalcone Ph-CH=CH-CO-Ph.

questions.q: Carboxylic acids are more acidic than phenols because
options: More resonance stabilisation of their conjugate base
questions.explanation: The carboxylate ion delocalises its negative charge equally over two equivalent oxygen atoms, giving greater resonance stabilisation than the phenoxide ion, making carboxylic acids more acidic.

questions.q: The compound that does not answer iodoform test is
questions.explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH$_3$CO- or CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; ethanoic acid (CH$_3$COOH) does not give a positive test, unlike ethanal, acetone and acetophenone.

questions.q: Oxidation of Toluene with chromyl chloride followed by hydrolysis gives Benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as ________
questions.explanation: Oxidation of a methylbenzene using CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ (chromyl chloride) followed by hydrolysis to give the aldehyde directly is called the Etard reaction.

questions.q: Statement-I: Reduction of ester by DIBAL-H followed by hydrolysis gives aldehyde. Statement-II: Oxidation of benzyl alcohol with aqueous KMnO$_4$ leads to the formation of Benzaldehyde. Among the above statements, identify the correct statement.
options: Both statements-I and II are true
Both statements-I and II are false
Statement-I is true but statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but statement-II is true
questions.explanation: DIBAL-H at low temperature reduces esters to aldehydes on hydrolysis (Statement-I true); but the strong oxidant KMnO$_4$ over-oxidises benzyl alcohol all the way to benzoic acid, not benzaldehyde (Statement-II false).

questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in their decreasing order of reactivity towards Nucleophilic addition reaction. CH$_3$COCH$_3$, CH$_3$COC$_2$H$_5$, CH$_3$CHO
questions.explanation: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition decreases with increasing steric bulk and decreasing positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, so aldehyde > methyl ketone > ethyl ketone: CH$_3$CHO > CH$_3$COCH$_3$ > CH$_3$COC$_2$H$_5$.

questions.q: Which of the following has most acidic Hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Each additional electron-withdrawing chlorine on the α-carbon further stabilises the carboxylate anion inductively, so trichloroacetic acid is the most acidic of the four.

questions.q: Propanone and Propanal are
questions.explanation: Propanone (a ketone) and propanal (an aldehyde) share the molecular formula C$_3$H$_6$O but have different functional groups, so they are functional isomers.

questions.q: Sodium ethanoate on heating with soda lime gives 'X'. Electrolysis of aqueous solution of sodium ethanoate gives 'Y'. 'X' and 'Y' respectively are
questions.explanation: CH$_3$COONa with soda lime undergoes decarboxylation to give CH$_4$ (X); Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous CH$_3$COONa gives C$_2$H$_6$ (Y) at the anode.

questions.q: In the reaction: C$_6$H$_5$CN $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ SnCl_2 + HCl}$ X $\xrightarrow{con.\,KOH}$ Y + Z, Formation of X, formation of Y and Z are known by
questions.explanation: SnCl$_2$/HCl followed by hydrolysis reduces the nitrile to benzaldehyde (X) via Stephen's reaction; benzaldehyde, having no alpha-hydrogen, undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated KOH to give benzyl alcohol (Y) and sodium benzoate (Z).

questions.q: Ethanoic acid undergoes Hell-Volhard Zelinsky reaction but Methanoic acid does not because of
options: absence of $\alpha$-H atom in ethanoic acid
presence of $\alpha$-H atom in methanoic acid
higher acidic strength of ethanoic acid than methanoic acid
presence of $\alpha$-H atom in ethanoic acid
questions.explanation: The HVZ reaction needs an $\alpha$-hydrogen. Methanoic acid (HCOOH) has no $\alpha$-carbon/$\alpha$-H, while ethanoic acid (CH$_3$COOH) does, so only ethanoic acid undergoes HVZ halogenation.

questions.q: The general name of the compound formed by the reaction between aldehyde and alcohol is
questions.explanation: An aldehyde reacts with two equivalents of alcohol (acid catalysed) to form a gem-dialkoxy compound called an acetal, RCH(OR')$_2$.

questions.q: Reaction by which benzaldehyde can NOT be prepared is
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg/conc. HCl) reduces a carbonyl group to $-$CH$_2-$; it cannot convert benzoic acid ($-$COOH) into benzaldehyde ($-$CHO), so option (D) is not a valid route to benzaldehyde.

questions.q: The test to differentiate between pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one is
questions.explanation: Pentan-2-one is a methyl ketone (CH$_3$CO-) and gives a positive iodoform test, whereas pentan-3-one lacks a CH$_3$CO- group and does not.

questions.q: An organic compound 'X' on treatment with PCC in dichloromethane gives the compound Y. Compound 'Y' reacts with I$_2$ and alkali to form yellow precipitate of triiodomethane. The compound X is
questions.explanation: PCC oxidises a primary alcohol only to an aldehyde. Since Y gives a positive iodoform test, Y is CH$_3$CHO, so X is ethanol (CH$_3$CH$_2$OH).

questions.q: In set of reactions, identify D: CH$_3$COOH $\xrightarrow{SOCl_2}$ A $\xrightarrow[Anh\ AlCl_3]{Benzene}$ B $\xrightarrow{HCN}$ C $\xrightarrow{H_2O}$ D
questions.explanation: A is CH$_3$COCl, B is acetophenone (from Friedel–Crafts acylation), C is the cyanohydrin of acetophenone, and D is its hydrolysis product, the α-hydroxy carboxylic acid (2-phenyl-2-hydroxypropanoic acid analogue).

questions.q: A $\xrightarrow[H_2O]{Hg SO_4/H_2SO_4}$, B $\xrightarrow{PCC}$, C $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_3O^+]{(i) SnCl_2/HCl}$ → Acetaldehyde. A, B and C respectively are
questions.explanation: Ethyne on Hg$^{2+}$/H$_2$SO$_4$ catalysed hydration gives acetaldehyde (A); PCC oxidises ethanol to acetaldehyde (B); Stephen reduction (SnCl$_2$/HCl then H$_3$O$^+$) converts ethanenitrile to acetaldehyde (C).

questions.q: The reagent which can do the conversion CH$_3$COOH → CH$_3$ – CH$_2$ – OH is
questions.explanation: LiAlH$_4$ is a strong reducing agent capable of reducing carboxylic acids directly to primary alcohols; NaBH$_4$ cannot reduce carboxylic acids.

questions.q: Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion? CH$_3$ – CH = CH – CH$_2$ – C(=O) – CH$_3$ $\rightarrow$ CH$_3$ – CH = CH – CH$_2$ – C(=O) –OH
options: I$_2$ and NaOH solution with subsequent acidification
questions.explanation: The haloform reaction (I$_2$/NaOH followed by acidification) selectively cleaves a methyl ketone to a carboxylic acid (losing one carbon as CHI$_3$) without affecting the C=C double bond.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde + CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(2)\ \Delta]{(1)\ \text{dil. NaOH}}$ P. The product 'P' is
options: C$_6$H$_5$-CH$_2$CHO (with an extra CHO on ring)
C$_6$H$_5$-CHO with a CH$_2$CHO substituent on ring
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no alpha-H, so acetaldehyde's alpha carbon attacks it in a cross aldol condensation; dehydration on heating gives cinnamaldehyde, C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH-CHO.

questions.q: The carbonyl compound that does not undergo aldol condensation is
questions.explanation: Trichloroacetaldehyde (Cl$_3$C-CHO) has no alpha-hydrogen atom, which is essential for aldol condensation.

questions.q:
Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion?
CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$-CO-CH$_3$ $\longrightarrow$ CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$-COOH
questions.explanation: I2/NaOH brings about the haloform reaction, converting the methyl ketone to a carboxylic acid (losing one carbon as CHI3) without touching the isolated C=C double bond.

questions.q: [Structure: HOCH$_2$-CH=CH-CHO is converted by three different reagents A, B, C respectively into (i) HOCH$_2$-CH=CH-CH$_2$OH (via A), (ii) OHC-CH=CH-CHO (via B), and (iii) HOCH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$OH, the saturated diol, via C.] The reagents A, B and C respectively are
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces the aldehyde to a primary alcohol without touching the alkene (A), PCC mildly oxidises the primary alcohol to an aldehyde, again leaving the alkene untouched (B), and H2/Pd catalytic hydrogenation reduces both the C=C double bond and the aldehyde, giving the saturated diol HOCH2CH2CH2CH2OH (C); matching option B.

questions.q: Propanoic acid undergoes HVZ reaction to give chloropropanoic acid. The product obtained is
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing Cl substituent introduced alpha to the carboxyl group by the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction stabilises the carboxylate anion inductively, making chloropropanoic acid a stronger acid than propanoic acid.

questions.q:
P $\xrightarrow{H_2/Pd-BaSO_4}$ Q $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ dil.\ HCl]{(i)\ con.\ NaOH}$ R + S.
R and S form benzyl benzoate when treated with each other. Hence P is
questions.explanation: Rosenmund reduction (H2/Pd-BaSO4) of benzoyl chloride (P) gives benzaldehyde (Q), which undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH to give benzyl alcohol (R) and sodium benzoate (giving benzoic acid, S, after acidification); R and S then esterify to form benzyl benzoate.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds undergoes haloform reaction ?
questions.explanation: Compounds with a CH$_3$CO- group, like acetone (CH$_3$COCH$_3$), undergo the haloform reaction with a halogen and base to give a haloform.

questions.q: The appropriate reagent for the following transformation is [a cyclic hydroxy-ketone converted to the corresponding hydroxy compound with -CH$_2$CH$_3$ in place of -COCH$_3$]
questions.explanation: The carbonyl group is reduced fully to -CH$_2$- while leaving the acid-sensitive -OH group untouched; this selective reduction is achieved by the Wolff-Kishner method (H$_2$N-NH$_2$, KOH/ethylene glycol), unlike the strongly acidic Clemmensen conditions.

questions.q: In the following reaction [toluene $\xrightarrow{CrO_2Cl_2/CS_2}$ X $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ Z] the compound Z is
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction: toluene's -CH$_3$ is oxidised by CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.

questions.q: Cannizzaro's reaction is an example of auto oxidation
options: It is a typical reaction of aliphatic aldehyde.
It is a reaction answered only by aromatic aldehydes.
It is a reaction answered by all aldehydes.
It is a reaction answered by only aldehydes containing α -hydrogen.
questions.explanation: Cannizzaro's (self oxidation-reduction) reaction is given by aldehydes lacking an α-hydrogen, typically aromatic aldehydes (and HCHO); since none of the options states this precisely, KEA awarded grace marks to all candidates (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Lower members of aliphatic carboxylic acid are soluble in water. This is due to
options: Formation of hydrogen bonds with water.
Van der-Waals interaction with water molecules.
questions.explanation: Lower aliphatic carboxylic acids form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, which makes them water-soluble.

questions.q: Reduction of ketones cannot be carried out with which of the following reagents ?
options: Sodium borohydride or Lithium Aluminium hydride
Hydrazine and KOH in ethylene glycol
Hydrogen in presence of palladium in Barium sulphate and quinoline
questions.explanation: H$_2$/Pd–BaSO$_4$/quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst) selectively reduces alkynes to alkenes and does not reduce the carbonyl group of ketones.

questions.q: Benzene carbaldehyde is reacted with concentrated NaOH solution to give the products A and B. The product A can be used food preservative and the product B is an aromatic hydroxy compound where OH group is linked to sp$^3$ hybridised carbon atom next to Benzene ring. The products A and B are respectively,
questions.explanation: This is the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde: it disproportionates in conc. NaOH to give sodium benzoate (A) and benzyl alcohol/phenylmethanol (B).

questions.q: An organic compound X is oxidised by using acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ solution. The product obtained reacts with phenyl hydrazine but does not answer silver mirror test. The compound X is,
questions.explanation: 2-Propanol is oxidised to acetone (a ketone), which forms a phenylhydrazone but gives a negative Tollens' (silver mirror) test, unlike an aldehyde.

questions.q: Predict the product 'C' in the following series of reactions : CH$_3$$-$COOH $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ A $\xrightarrow[\text{Anhyd AlCl}_3]{\text{C}_6\text{H}_6}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}}$ C
questions.explanation: A = CH$_3$COCl, B = acetophenone (C$_6$H$_5$COCH$_3$) via Friedel-Crafts acylation, and Grignard addition of CH$_3$MgBr to the ketone gives the tertiary alcohol (CH$_3$)$_2$C(OH)C$_6$H$_5$ (grace mark was awarded for this question).

questions.q: The distinguishing test between methanoic acid and ethanoic acid is
questions.explanation: Methanoic (formic) acid has an aldehydic -CHO group and gives a positive Tollens' silver-mirror test, while ethanoic (acetic) acid does not, so Tollens' test distinguishes them.

questions.q: The formation of cyanohydrin from a ketone is an example of
questions.explanation: The cyanide ion (a nucleophile) adds across the polar C=O bond of the ketone to give a cyanohydrin, which is a nucleophilic addition reaction.

questions.q: Iodoform can be prepared from all, except
questions.explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH$_3$CO- group or a CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; propan-1-ol (a primary alcohol without this arrangement) does not give a positive iodoform test, unlike the other three compounds.

questions.q: Acetic acid is treated with Ca(OH)$_2$ and the product so obtained is subjected to dry distillation. The final product is
questions.explanation: Acetic acid with Ca(OH)$_2$ forms calcium acetate, which on dry distillation undergoes ketonic decarboxylation to give propanone (acetone).

questions.q: Acetophenone cannot be prepared easily starting from
questions.explanation: Benzene gives acetophenone by Friedel-Crafts acylation, phenylacetylene by Markovnikov hydration, and 1-phenylethanol by mild oxidation; toluene has no easy direct route to acetophenone.

questions.q: Iodoform reaction is answered by all, except
questions.explanation: The iodoform test requires a CH$_3$CO- group or a CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; 1-propanol (CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH) has neither and does not give a positive iodoform test, unlike ethanol, acetaldehyde, and the given hydroxy acid.

questions.q:
Match the reactant in Column – I with the reaction in Column – II:

Column I: (i) Acetic acid (ii) Sodium phenate (iii) Methyl cyanide (iv) Toluene

Column II: (a) Stephen (b) Friedel-Crafts (c) HVZ (d) Kolbe's
options: i – c, ii – d, iii – a, iv – b
i – b, ii – c, iii – a, iv – d
i – d, ii – b, iii – c, iv – a
i – c, ii – a, iii – d, iv – b
questions.explanation: Acetic acid undergoes the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction; sodium phenate undergoes Kolbe's reaction; methyl cyanide (a nitrile) is reduced via the Stephen reaction to an aldehyde; toluene undergoes Friedel-Crafts type reactions — matching i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b.

questions.q:
The acid strength of active methylene group in

(a) CH$_3$COCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$

(b) CH$_3$COCH$_2$COCH$_3$

(c) C$_2$H$_5$OOCCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$ decreases as
questions.explanation: Diketone (b, CH$_3$COCH$_2$COCH$_3$) with two strongly electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups is most acidic, keto-ester (a, CH$_3$COCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$) is intermediate, and diester (c, C$_2$H$_5$OOCCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$) with two weaker-withdrawing ester groups is least acidic; so acid strength decreases as b > a > c.

questions.q:
P $\xrightarrow[2. H_3O^+]{1. CH_3MgBr}$ R $\xrightarrow[2. \Delta]{1. dil.\ NaOH}$ 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one

P is
questions.explanation: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one is formed by aldol condensation of two acetone molecules; R (the aldol product before dehydration) is 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one, which comes from acetone reacting with CH$_3$MgBr followed by hydrolysis of the resulting imine/nitrile addition product — P is ethanenitrile (CH$_3$CN), which with CH$_3$MgBr and hydrolysis gives acetone (R's precursor).

questions.q: When formic acid is heated with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: Conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ dehydrates formic acid (HCOOH) to release only CO gas.

questions.q: The compound formed when calcium acetate and calcium formate is dry distilled.
questions.explanation: Dry distillation of a mixture of calcium acetate and calcium formate gives a mixed ketone-type reaction that yields acetaldehyde.

questions.q: The reagent used to distinguish between acetaldehyde and benzaldehyde is
questions.explanation: Fehling's solution gives a positive test (red precipitate) only with aliphatic aldehydes like acetaldehyde, not with benzaldehyde, so it distinguishes the two.

questions.q: Oil of winter green is
questions.explanation: Oil of wintergreen is methyl salicylate, an ester of salicylic acid.

questions.q: An organic compound 'A' burns with a sooty flame. It is negative towards Tollen's reagent test and positive for Borsche's reagent test. The compound 'A' is
questions.explanation: A sooty flame indicates an aromatic compound; a negative Tollen's test rules out an aldehyde, and a positive Borsche's reagent test (for aromatic methyl ketones) identifies it as acetophenone.

questions.q: HCHO was treated with a reagent X. The product formed upon hydrolysis in the presence of an acid gave C$_2$H$_5$OH. The reagent X is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$MgI (Grignard reagent) reacts with HCHO to form CH$_3$CH$_2$OMgI, which on acid hydrolysis gives ethanol (C$_2$H$_5$OH).

questions.q: The relative acidic strengths of benzoic acid, o-toluic acid and p-toluic acid is of the decreasing order:
options: p-toluic acid > o-toluic acid > benzoic acid
o-toluic acid > p-toluic acid > benzoic acid
p-toluic acid > benzoic acid > o-toluic acid
o-toluic acid > benzoic acid > p-toluic acid
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group decreases acidity relative to benzoic acid, and the ortho effect makes o-toluic acid more acidic than p-toluic acid, giving the order o-toluic acid > benzoic acid > p-toluic acid.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH$_3$-CH(OH)-CH$_2$-CHO [pent-2-... structure with OH and C=O] is
questions.explanation: The compound is a pentanone chain with a ketone at C2 and hydroxyl at C4; the principal characteristic group (ketone) gets the lowest locant, giving 4-hydroxy-2-pentanone.

questions.q: Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. This can be explained using ..........
questions.explanation: The methyl group in acetic acid exerts a +I (electron-donating) effect that destabilizes its conjugate base, making acetic acid weaker than formic acid, which lacks this alkyl group.

questions.q: The reagent with which both acetaldehyde and acetone react is ..............
questions.explanation: Both acetaldehyde and acetone contain a $CH_3CO-$ group and give a positive iodoform test with $I_2/NaOH$; Fehling's and Tollens' reagents react only with aldehydes, not ketones.

questions.q: Which of the following gives an aldehyde on dry distillation?
questions.explanation: Dry distillation of a mixture of calcium formate and calcium acetate gives acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$) along with calcium carbonate.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of $CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-COOH$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Numbering from the carboxylic acid carbon (C1) gives $CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-COOH$ as but-3-enoic acid, with the double bond between C3 and C4.

questions.q: The compound obtained when acetaldehyde reacts with dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide exhibits ...............
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation gives 3-hydroxybutanal, CH$_3$CH(OH)CH$_2$CHO, which has one chiral carbon and hence shows optical isomerism, but no C=C stereocentre for geometric isomerism.

questions.q: Chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. This can be explained using .........
questions.explanation: The electronegative chlorine withdraws electron density inductively (-I effect), stabilizing the conjugate base and increasing acidity.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde and acetone can be best distinguished using ...............
questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with benzaldehyde (an aldehyde) but not with acetone (a ketone); Fehling's solution and 2,4-DNPH do not distinguish them (aromatic aldehydes don't reduce Fehling's, and both give a 2,4-DNPH precipitate).

questions.q: The correct sequence of steps involved in the mechanism of Cannizzaro's reaction is .......
options: transfer of $H^-$, transfer of $H^+$ and nucleophilic attack
nucleophilic attack, transfer of $H^-$ and transfer of $H^+$
electrophilic attack by $OH^-$, transfer of $H^+$ and transfer of $H^-$
transfer of $H^+$, nucleophilic attack and transfer of $H^-$
questions.explanation: OH$^-$ first adds (nucleophilic attack) to one aldehyde molecule, the resulting intermediate transfers a hydride (H$^-$) to a second aldehyde molecule, and finally a proton (H$^+$) is transferred to give the alcohol and carboxylate.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [CH$_3$CH$_2$-CHBr-CH(CH$_3$)-CHO, drawn as a skeletal structure with CHO at one end, a methyl branch at C2 and Br at C3] is ......................
questions.explanation: The longest chain including the CHO carbon has 5 carbons (pentanal) with a methyl at C2 and Br at C3, giving 3-bromo-2-methylpentanal.

questions.q: CH$_3$COOH $\xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$ X $\xrightarrow[300°C]{\text{Cu}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{dilute NaOH}}$ Z. In the above reaction Z is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$COOH is reduced to ethanol (X), dehydrogenated over Cu to acetaldehyde (Y), which undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH to give aldol (Z).

questions.q: The compound which is not formed during the dry distillation of a mixture of calcium formate and calcium acetate is
questions.explanation: Cross/self ketonic decarboxylation gives methanal (formate+formate), ethanal (formate+acetate) and propanone (acetate+acetate); propanal would need a propionate salt, which is absent.

questions.q: The reaction involved in the oil of Winter Green test is Salicylic acid $\xrightarrow[\text{Conc. } H_2SO_4]{\Delta}$ product. The product is treated with Na$_2$CO$_3$ solution. The missing reagent in the above reaction is
questions.explanation: Salicylic acid esterifies with methanol (conc. H$_2$SO$_4$, heat) to give methyl salicylate, 'oil of wintergreen'.
